chunks: Fadalah ibn Abi al-Maghra' said: Ya'qub al-Ahmar narrated to me saying, 'I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) to console him for Ismail.'

He invoked mercy upon him, then said: 'Verily Allah consoled His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) Himself, saying: "Verily you shall die, and they will die too" (Q39:30). And He said: "Every soul will taste death" (Q3:195).'

Then he began speaking and said: 'Indeed, the inhabitants of the earth will die until no one remains. Then the inhabitants of the heavens will die until no one remains except the Angel of Death, the bearers of the Throne, Jibra'il, and Mika'il.'

Then the Angel of Death comes and stands before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, and it is said to him, 'Who has remained?' (while He knows better). He replies, 'O Lord, no one remains except the Angel of Death, the bearers of the Throne, Jibra'il, and Mika'il.'

He is told, 'Command Jibra'il and Mika'il to die.' So the angels say, 'O Lord, they are Your messengers and Your trusted ones!' He says, 'I have decreed for every soul possessing the spirit that it must die.'

Then the Angel of Death comes and stands before Allah, the Almighty, and it is said to him, 'Who has remained?' (while He knows better). He replies, 'O Lord, no one remains except the Angel of Death and the bearers of the Throne.'

He is told, 'Command the bearers of the Throne to die.' Then the Angel of Death comes with his gaze lowered. He is asked, 'Who has remained?' So he says, 'O Lord, no one remains except the Angel of Death.'

He says to him, 'Die, O Angel of Death!' So he dies. Then He takes the earth in His left hand and the heavens in His right hand, shaking them severely many times. Then He says, 'Where are those who used to invoke associates with Me? Where are those who placed with Me another deity?'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the angels and the universe after everyone else has died?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* elaborates on the concept of *Mawt al-Nafs* (death of the soul) beyond the physical end, detailing a cosmic sequence where all creation, including the archangels Jibra'il and Mika'il and the bearers of the Throne, succumb to death. It highlights the unique status of the Angel of Death as the final entity to perish, after which Allah shakes the heavens and earth to question the polytheists, reinforcing the transient nature of all existence except the Divine. This narrative serves as a profound reminder of *Tawhid* (monotheism) and the ultimate futility of worldly power in the face of Allah's absolute decree.
